title: Prevent cursor stalls when WindowServer applies events late
description: Under extreme host/WindowServer load CGEventPost returns quickly but the live Quartz position remains stale. Absolute moves are repeatedly based on the same old position and coalescing loses movement. Accumulate a bounded target, reset on reversal/idle/display change, and retain the screen-edge no-catch-up behavior.
design: Accumulate intended absolute target inside the connected active-display topology, but let the asynchronous delivery worker recompute from the latest live cursor and emit at most 24px per event (one normal high-speed tick). Coalesce to the newest target without crossing button commands. Reset planner target when neutral increments movement generation; reversal, idle, and display epoch also resync. Never call synchronous cursor warp from the realtime performer.
acceptance_criteria: Delivery step never exceeds 24px even when target is far; full target preserves configured speed while held; neutral generation discards queued and planner-side target so no catch-up tail resumes; display gaps cannot be crossed but touching displays can; no realtime recovery warps; delivery step/post/cancellation metrics persist; workspace tests and live-load verification pass.
notes: Aug 20 root incident: load avg 233+, WindowServer CGEventPost blocked 50-365ms. False recovery warps blocked performer up to 273ms. Removing warps exposed unbounded absolute jumps up to 1156px. A 32px planner cap prevented teleports but fired on ~75% of ticks and reduced speed. Latest PID 69137 (13:03) keeps the full target for normal velocity but delivery recomputes from live cursor and emits <=24px, while neutral generation resets both queue and planner target. Added delivery_step_px/limited plus existing post, queue, cursor and generation metrics. IOHID relative transport was investigated, but IOHIDPostEvent access is currently denied; non-coalesced CGEvents remain rejected because prior history showed a stale tail after release. 37 control tests plus workspace suite pass; awaiting active-stick live window and subjective confirmation.

title: Add browser trackpad scroll mode
description: Add a dedicated two-axis continuous pixel-scroll stick mode for browser canvases such as Miro. Emit one diagonal trackpad-style event per tick, coalesce it under load, and enable it for every configured browser without changing ordinary app scrolling.
design: Final controls: right stick pans; RT is the trackpad zoom modifier; RB remains the existing voice/right-Command binding; LT is the only analog speed boost for browser trackpad mode. trigger_scroll_boost excludes whichever trigger is configured as zoom_button so zoom activation cannot simultaneously apply the 6x boost.
acceptance_criteria: Profile parses mode trackpad_scroll; diagonal joystick input produces one two-axis continuous pixel scroll event; worker coalesces queued trackpad deltas; all configured browser bundle IDs override the right stick with trackpad_scroll; profile hot-reloads and live daemon remains healthy.
notes: Added red/green regression test proving an RT zoom modifier excludes RT from boost selection; LT at 0.5 wins even when RT is fully pressed. padjutsud lib tests (13) and strict clippy pass; signed release build passes. Ready for rollout.

title: Fix click warp and cursor edge overshoot after display changes
description: After main display changed from the launch-time 1512x982 display to a 2560x1440 display, Enigo click events still convert NSEvent.mouseLocation using the cached old CGDisplay height, shifting click Y by about 458 px. Relative move events also write raw delta fields beyond screen edges, creating invisible overshoot that must be reversed before the visible cursor moves.
design: On macOS route click, double-click, press, and release through a native Quartz path that snapshots CGEvent.location and posts the button event at that exact global point. Never call Enigo::location for buttons. Relative movement continues to use absolute destination but explicitly publishes deltaX=deltaY=0 so WindowServer cannot accumulate hidden relative motion beyond a clamped display edge.
acceptance_criteria: Mouse click/press/release use live native Quartz cursor coordinates and never depend on cached display geometry; movement events do not accumulate relative deltas past screen boundaries; regression tests cover click location and zero movement-delta fields; existing display callback metrics remain; live daemon validates clicks and immediate reverse movement at every display edge.
notes: Live diagnosis after display epoch 2: current main display 2560x1440, cached launch-time Enigo display 1512x982, causing about 458px click Y error. Quartz constructor probe confirmed absolute mouse events default to zero relative deltas. TDD red/green tests cover live click point and zero edge deltas. padjutsu-control 28 tests, strict control clippy, full workspace suite, release build, and codesign pass. Ready for rollout.

title: Fix cursor pinning after display reconfiguration
description: Long-lived daemon uses NSEvent.mouseLocation plus cached main display height to convert AppKit coordinates to Quartz. After display layout changes, observed live values were NSEvent=(857,-4801), CGEvent=(757,981.98), active display bounds=(0,0,1512,982), causing every destination Y to clamp to the bottom. Remove AppKit coordinate conversion and react to CGDisplay reconfiguration callbacks without polling display geometry in the mouse hot path.
design: Use CGEvent::new(...).location() as the live cursor source in native Quartz coordinates. Register CGDisplayRegisterReconfigurationCallback once when Performer is created; callback only advances an atomic epoch after completed changes, with no display-geometry query in the mouse hot path. Expose epoch and observed callback count in production performer metrics and reset the cursor-tracking baseline across reconfiguration events.
acceptance_criteria: Vertical and horizontal joystick movement remain correct after monitor attach/detach or layout changes; mouse hot path performs no NSScreen or CGDisplay geometry polling; production metrics expose display_epoch and display_reconfiguration_events; control tests and strict clippy pass.
notes: Implemented, tested, installed, and restarted on 2026-08-05. cargo test -p padjutsu-control: 22 passed; strict control clippy passed. Normal SIGTERM was ignored by the old process, so it was terminated with SIGKILL and launchd restarted it. Old PID 55233; new PID 70265, started 11:47:43 +05. codesign verification passed; launchd state is running; installed binary contains display_reconfiguration_events metric. Awaiting live joystick confirmation before closing.

title: Prevent duplicate gamepad actions when release is delayed under load
description: A single physical press can execute twice under host load. A queued/dropped release can let a keystroke repeat fire after the physical button is already up; chord repeats were keyed by the button completing the chord, so releasing another chord member failed to cancel the task.
design: Maintain authoritative per-controller button snapshots in the SDL runtime independently of the bounded subscriber queue. Before each timer wake, cancel repeat tasks whose full binding mask is no longer physically held. Key start/stop of repeat tasks by the full rule target mask.
acceptance_criteria: Physical release cancels repeat before a delayed queued release is consumed; chord start/release address the same repeat task; cancellation is persisted in production wake metrics; regression tests pass; live duplicate report is not reproduced.
notes: Implemented and deployed in PID 34529 at 12:45 on Aug 20. New metric: button_repeat_snapshot_cancellations; incident cause: stale-button-repeat-cancelled. Workspace tests pass; awaiting live confirmation.

title: Reduce macOS pointer latency under system load
description: Migrate issue tracking from the empty bd/Dolt scaffold to br. Remove the per-tick display geometry query from relative mouse movement without caching cursor position, add low-overhead performer latency metrics, quiet hot INFO logs, and verify the installed daemon under load.
acceptance_criteria: Relative cursor movement remains smooth under load; cursor position is read live rather than cached; PADJUTSU_METRICS exposes queue and execution latency; default logs do not grow at tick rate; crate tests, clippy, and release build pass.
notes: Verified live on macOS at load averages 68-121. Performer queue wait p99 approximately 50us, mouse post p99 0.25-0.5ms, queue_len=0, max_batch=2-3; 15-second sample showed no SLSGetDisplayBounds in the movement hot path. Scoped Clippy passed; padjutsu-control 15/15 and padjutsud 38/38 tests passed; signed release installed. Added just measure-latency for repeatable measurement.
close_reason: Completed: live stress measurement passed, signed release installed, diagnostics command verified.

title: Prevent mouse tail after stick release
description: Under system load, cursor can continue moving after the stick returns to neutral. Production metrics show no daemon queue backlog or subscriber drops but large cursor tracking error. macOS movement events are explicitly marked non-coalesced, allowing WindowServer to queue and replay stale motion.
acceptance_criteria: MouseMoved events remain coalescible; regression test prevents restoring non-coalesced flags; release builds and installed launchd daemon runs.
notes: Reopened after immediate recurrence. Fresh metrics isolated two upstream tails despite queue_len=0: dense historical AxisMotion bursts (p50 <=250us) and a 242.9ms CGEventPost stall that accumulated 8 commands into a 125px delta. Implemented authoritative latest-axis snapshots updated before subscriber delivery and polled from SDL every 8ms; sync before every tick; neutral hard-resets smoothing and increments a worker movement generation to invalidate queued commands; catch-up delta is capped at 32px. Tests cover full subscriber queue, neutral snapshot correction, neutral smoothing stop, generation invalidation, and catch-up cap. Live 5s verification under load: axis_snapshot_corrections=81, clamped_mouse_posts=4, mouse delta max=32px, queue_len=0. Awaiting user confirmation before closing.

title: Add persistent metrics flight recorder
description: Always-on nonblocking timestamped metrics history with bounded rotation, incident markers, and time-window CLI queries.
design: Shared padjutsu-metrics crate; 5s aggregate snapshots; bounded sync_channel/try_send from hot paths; one background JSONL writer; 32MiB x 8 total files; CLI window reader and incident classifier.
acceptance_criteria: Production daemon records timestamped gamepad/wake/stick/performer metrics without blocking input; history survives restarts and rotates within 256MiB; CLI supports recent/time-centered/incident-only queries and markers; live launchd smoke test succeeds.
notes: Verified on live launchd PID 34194. Recorder captured gamepad, wake, stick and performer snapshots, including a 7.3ms performer queue wait, 5.8ms wake lateness, one missed stick period, and cursor tracking stall. CLI classifier returned the corresponding causes.

title: Preserve pixel-scroll speed semantics
description: Trackpad scroll refactor explicitly writes SCROLL_WHEEL_EVENT_IS_CONTINUOUS=0 for ordinary pixel scroll events. Quartz creates pixel events with continuous=1 by default; overriding it makes apps interpret the same deltas as wheel steps and changes perceived speed.
design: Represent the continuous field as an optional override. Ordinary pixel scroll leaves SCROLL_WHEEL_EVENT_IS_CONTINUOUS untouched so Quartz retains its constructor default (verified live as 1 for pixel units); trackpad scroll explicitly sets Some(true).
acceptance_criteria: Ordinary smooth pixel scroll preserves Quartz constructor continuous semantics; trackpad_scroll explicitly remains continuous; regression tests cover both paths; existing configured speed feels unchanged outside browser canvases.
notes: TDD red captured bool/Option mismatch for the desired no-override path. Green: padjutsu-control 26 tests pass and strict control clippy passes. Ready for rollout.

title: Add production jerk diagnostics
description: Keep low-overhead metrics enabled in release builds and distinguish pointer jerks caused by scheduler stalls, performer queueing/coalescing, large output deltas, irregular post cadence, or slow CGEvent posting.
acceptance_criteria: Production mode reports at a configurable low frequency; tick and mouse-post histograms expose p95/p99/max, missed periods, coalescing and large deltas; anomaly counters do not spam logs; release build and scoped tests pass; live daemon is verified.
notes: Implemented default-on 60s production metrics for SDL loop gaps/drops/broadcast cost, wake deadline lateness, stick tick cadence/execution/missed periods, performer queue wait/coalescing/deltas/input age, CGEvent post latency with >4/>16/>50ms counters, and cursor tracking error. Live diagnostics found and fixed stale tick dt after idle/deadzone (pre-fix max 91.686ms; post-fix nominal 8ms resume). A live loaded run then isolated a rare 86.068ms mouse post stall that backed up the performer queue; subsequent verification showed no >16ms mouse posts, zero queue waits >4ms, zero drops, wake p99 <=250us, and explicit anomaly counters. Release installed/codesigned and launchd PID verified. Scoped tests and clippy passed. Install now uses --locked; measurement tolerates unavailable macOS sample.
close_reason: Production jerk diagnostics implemented, live-validated, and installed

title: Handle atomic profile saves in macOS watcher
description: macOS FsEventWatcher missed repeated apply_patch-style atomic saves of the canonical gc_profile.yaml. No profile changed/error event was emitted after saves at 12:05:54 and 12:06+, although startup reload works. Investigate directory-level FSEvents/temp rename paths and reload on relevant directory events without polling.
acceptance_criteria: Atomic temp-file+rename saves of gc_profile.yaml trigger exactly one successful profile reload on macOS; unrelated files in the watched directory do not reload the profile; watcher tests cover direct writes and atomic replacement.

title: Add virtual HID mouse backend
description: Replace the latency-prone Quartz CGEventPost movement path with a TDD-specified virtual HID mouse backend. Cover report descriptor/encoding, relative motion chunking, persistent button state, transport failures, runtime selection, metrics, and Quartz fallback. Do not switch production default until the native backend is verified on this Mac.
design: Virtual HID contract: 5-byte report [buttons, signed dx, signed dy, signed wheel, signed pan]; five stable pointer-button bits; deltas outside -127..127 are emitted as ordered chunks; zero deltas emit nothing; button state changes are transactional with transport success; clicks are ordered press/release pairs. macOS movement/buttons select the backend through PADJUTSU_MOUSE_BACKEND, defaulting to Quartz.
notes: Implemented and live-verified virtual HID mouse delivery through the installed Karabiner DriverKit VirtualHIDDevice. Added a TDD-covered protocol crate and root LaunchDaemon bridge, bounded coalescing that preserves button transitions, reconnecting 5-byte client transport without per-report ACK, explicit Quartz fallback, automatic HID preference, reproducible just install-hid-bridge, and time-constraint scheduling for the padjutsud delivery thread. Fixed Darwin sub-second SO_RCVTIMEO session teardown discovered during live testing. Stress evidence at host load ~82 and ~19 GB swap: three consecutive windows had transport avg 14-15us, p99 25us, max 37us; measured end-to-end max 89us; queue=0, dropped=0, missed stick periods=0. Validation: padjutsu-hid-bridge 8/8, padjutsu-control 52/52, clippy -D warnings for both crates, release build and codesign, plist lint, live LaunchDaemon/backend verification.
